stem: A client with known peptic ulcer disease develops sudden severe abdominal pain with a rigid, boardlike abdomen. Which complication should the nurse suspect?
rationale: Bowel/gastrointestinal perforation can present with sudden severe abdominal pain and peritoneal signs such as guarding or rigidity. Peptic ulcer disease is a recognized cause of upper gastrointestinal perforation.
educational_objective: Recognize perforation and peritonitis as an emergency complication of peptic ulcer disease.
source_organization: National Library of Medicine / NCBI Bookshelf (StatPearls)
source_locator: Etiology includes peptic ulcer disease; clinical presentation includes acute severe abdominal pain and peritoneal signs/rigidity
source_claim_supported: Peptic ulcer disease can cause GI perforation, which may present with sudden severe pain and peritoneal rigidity.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
correction_summary: Replaced a mismatched ACG/WSES citation with a current NCBI source directly supporting perforation signs and PUD as an etiology.
